note: Four anti-IL-33 antibodies (etokimab, itepekimab, torudokimab, tozorakimab) entered moderate-to-severe AD on IL-33-transgenic and IL-33/ST2-knockout MC903 mouse data, an IL1RL1 GWAS locus and a 12-patient etokimab challenge study; all four missed their phase 2 primary endpoint between 2019 and 2022 while the COPD programs continued.
label: Atopic eczema (anti-IL-33)

engagement.note: K14-IL-33 transgenic mice develop itchy eczema with eosinophils, IL-5/IL-13 and ILC2 expansion; no dosed-human PD comparison yet.
engagement.quote: Furthermore, the proportion of group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s), which produce IL-5, were significantly increased in the lesional skin, peripheral blood, and regional lymph nodes.
engagement.judgement: Opens the mouse track at 2013: Imai 2013 (August) and Salimi 2013 (December) are the first IL-33/ST2 AD-model papers; the PD readouts they carry forward are blood eosinophils, IL-5/IL-13 and skin ILC2s. None of the four antibodies binds mouse IL-33 (stated for torudokimab in Okragly 2021), so product_in_model is false throughout.

engagement.model: IL1RL1 AD-GWAS locus and IL33 loss-of-function carriers
engagement.note: A rare IL33 splice variant lowers blood eosinophils and halves asthma risk; the eosinophil readout is what the antibodies could later be checked against.
engagement.quote: rs146597587-C associates with lower eosinophil counts (β = -0.21 SD, P = 2.5×10-16, N = 103,104), and reduced risk of asthma in Europeans (OR = 0.47; 95%CI: 0.32, 0.70, P = 1.8×10-4, N cases = 6,465, N controls = 302,977).
engagement.judgement: The genetics track first appears in AD at Hirota 2012 (efficacy cell); the eosinophil PD prediction only arrives with the IL33 loss-of-function variant in 2017, so this cell's track opens here. Asthma and eosinophils, not AD, are the phenotypes in the source.

engagement.note: A single systemic etokimab dose lowered peripheral eosinophils by day 29 in 12 AD patients, the readout the IL-33 mice used.
engagement.short: Etokimab lowers eosinophils in AD patients
engagement.quote: Rapid and sustained clinical benefit was observed, with 83% achieving Eczema Area and Severity Index 50 (EASI50), and 33% EASI75, with reduction in peripheral eosinophils at day 29 after administration.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; 12 patients, single dose, eosinophil change is vs baseline rather than vs placebo; the paper invokes 'genetic and functional associations', not the mouse data, so the pairing is mine.
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison: the transgenic/knockout mice predicted eosinophil and type-2 readouts move with IL-33; they did in dosed AD patients. Direction only, no magnitude available at abstract level.
engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral blood eosinophil count, day 29 vs baseline

engagement.model: House-dust-mite skin challenge in AD patients (single-dose etokimab)
engagement.note: Placebo-controlled house-dust-mite skin challenge in the same 12 patients: etokimab cut neutrophil infiltration into challenged skin.
engagement.short: HDM-challenge skin neutrophils fell vs placebo
engagement.quote: We noted significant reduction in skin neutrophil infiltration after etokimab compared with placebo upon skin challenge with house dust mite, reactivity to which has been implicated in the pathogenesis of AD.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the challenge arm was placebo-controlled but the trial was 12 patients and one dose; no registry record found for this study, so registry_date is null.
engagement.judgement: Scored on its own track as a human challenge system (track identity rule): model and dosed humans are the same study, so comparison_stated is true; the readout is downstream of IL-33. Chinthrajah 2019 (JCI Insight, doi:10.1172/jci.insight.131347, NCT02920021) adds the same molecule reducing skin-prick reactivity and peanut-specific IgE in peanut allergy, but that is another disease and is not scored here.
engagement.magnitude_basis: HDM-evoked skin neutrophil infiltration vs placebo

engagement.model: IL1RL1 AD-GWAS locus and IL33 loss-of-function carriers
engagement.note: The eosinophil fall the IL33 loss-of-function carriers predicted was reproduced by one etokimab dose in AD patients.
engagement.quote: Rapid and sustained clinical benefit was observed, with 83% achieving Eczema Area and Severity Index 50 (EASI50), and 33% EASI75, with reduction in peripheral eosinophils at day 29 after administration.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; same 12-patient source as the mouse-track entry; Kosloski 2024 later confirmed the eosinophil decrease with itepekimab at target-saturating doses.
engagement.judgement: Paired myself: Smith 2017 predicted that losing IL-33 lowers blood eosinophils; antibody neutralization did the same in AD patients (Chen 2019) and again with itepekimab (Kosloski 2024). This is the one prediction on the genetics track that held.
engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral blood eosinophil count, day 29 vs baseline
engagement.reason: Genetic eosinophil prediction held in patients

engagement.note: Itepekimab saturated serum total IL-33 at 300 mg q4w/q2w and lowered blood eosinophils in two phase 2 AD trials.
engagement.quote: Pharmacodynamics of total IL-33 indicated that itepekimab saturated binding to the target in serum at 300 mg q2w and q4w doses, and decreased blood eosinophil counts.
engagement.judgement: Strengthens the 2019 match with a direct readout (target saturation in serum) from the two terminated itepekimab trials (NCT03738423, results posted 2022-06-10; NCT03736967). Caveat from Chen 2026 (MAbs, doi:10.1080/19420862.2026.2639673): etokimab and itepekimab bind epitope 2 and only partially block ST2 engagement in cells, so serum saturation may overstate pathway blockade.
engagement.magnitude_basis: serum total IL-33 (target-mediated accumulation) and blood eosinophils
engagement.reason: Target saturated, eosinophils fell, no efficacy

engagement.model: Anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody in DNCB-induced AD mice (Peng 2018)
engagement.note: Antibody blockade in DNCB mice cut lesional eosinophil and mast-cell infiltration and serum IgE; none of these readouts was posted from an anti-IL-33 AD trial.
engagement.short: DNCB mice: skin eosinophils, IgE fell
engagement.quote: Eosinophils and mast cells infiltration and serum IgE levels were also significantly reduced by αIL-33Ab.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Springer, paywalled). Blood eosinophils fell in dosed patients (Chen 2019; Kosloski 2024), but the model's readouts were lesional infiltrates and serum IgE, neither posted for a member's AD trial (NCT03533751, NCT03738423, NCT03831191 outcome lists), so no pairing was made.
engagement.judgement: Own track: a dosed neutralising antibody in a hapten (DNCB) model is a different system from the MC903 transgenic/knockout track and makes a different kind of prediction (pharmacological, not genetic). Untested rather than same: the compartment differs (skin infiltrate vs blood count) and serum IgE was not reported in any AD trial of the four members.

engagement.model: Human-IL-33-challenge mouse PD assay, IL-5 endpoint (torudokimab)
engagement.note: Torudokimab blocked human-IL-33-driven IL-5 in mice; no IL-5 or other PD readout was posted for any torudokimab trial, so the assay was never checked against dosed humans.
engagement.short: Mouse IL-5 PD assay, no human PD
engagement.quote: followed by an in vivo IL-33-induced pharmacodynamic inhibition assay in mice that used IL-5 production as the endpoint.
engagement.confidence_note: Open access, abstract and methods statement; the assay predates the 2017-11 first-in-human study (NCT03343587) but 2021 is its first public date, matching the draft's dating of the same paper's cyno track. ClinicalTrials.gov outcome lists for NCT03343587, NCT03831191 and NCT03913260 carry PK, safety and efficacy only; Laquer 2022 (research letter, paywalled) not opened.
engagement.judgement: Own engagement track, distinct from the draft's cyno specificity/PK safety track built on the same paper: a human-cytokine challenge in mice with the member antibody dosed (product_in_model true, the only member ever given to an animal in print) and an IL-5 endpoint. No dosed-human IL-5 datum exists for torudokimab, so untested.

engagement.model: In-vitro neutrophil migration to skin interstitial fluid (etokimab)
engagement.note: Etokimab blocked human neutrophil migration toward skin interstitial fluid in vitro; the readout is neutrophil chemotaxis, downstream of IL-33.
engagement.short: Etokimab blocks neutrophil migration in vitro
engagement.quote: We showed that etokimab also inhibited neutrophil migration to skin interstitial fluid in vitro.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (STM paywalled; no Europe PMC manuscript). Source of the interstitial fluid (patients' challenged skin or not) and assay format are not in the abstract.
engagement.judgement: Own ex_vivo track, not folded into the HDM-challenge track: a human-cell chemotaxis assay with the product present is a different system from a placebo-controlled challenge in dosed patients, and the draft keeps systems apart. Opens untested in the same year and source as its comparison, per the brief's opener rule.

engagement.model: In-vitro neutrophil migration to skin interstitial fluid (etokimab)
engagement.note: The in-vitro block of neutrophil migration was matched in the same 12 patients: etokimab cut neutrophil infiltration into HDM-challenged skin versus placebo.
engagement.short: In-vitro block matched in challenged skin
engagement.quote: We noted significant reduction in skin neutrophil infiltration after etokimab compared with placebo upon skin challenge with house dust mite, reactivity to which has been implicated in the pathogenesis of AD.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only; 12 patients, single dose. The abstract does not say whether the in-vitro assay ran before or after the in-vivo readout: if it was run on post-dose fluid it is a concurrent mechanistic check, not a prospective prediction, and would score retro rather than same.
engagement.judgement: comparison_stated true: the source itself sets the in-vitro block beside the in-vivo neutrophil reduction. Downstream readout (neutrophil chemotaxis/infiltration), direction only. Scored same, not retro, because the ordering is unknown and the brief's engagement question explicitly admits ex-vivo blockade of a stimulus; flagged for the checker.
engagement.magnitude_basis: skin neutrophil infiltration after HDM challenge, etokimab vs placebo (direction; numbers not in the abstract)

engagement.model: Anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody in DNCB-induced AD mice (Peng 2018)
engagement.note: One 300 mg etokimab dose left serum total IgE unchanged at day 29 and day 140 in 12 AD patients, where antibody-dosed DNCB mice had lowered serum IgE.
engagement.short: Mouse IgE fell; patients' IgE unchanged
engagement.quote: There was no significant change in serum total IgE during the study
engagement.confidence_note: Read in the Oxford accepted manuscript (ORA uuid:5e031a33): open-label single dose, 12 patients, no placebo arm for IgE; means 10101 to 9954 kU/L at day 29. Blood eosinophils did fall (draft's mouse-track entry), so the miss is readout-specific.
engagement.judgement: Paired myself: Chen 2019 cites Peng's decreased serum IgE in its discussion but does not set it against its own null IgE result. The model's serum-IgE prediction did not reproduce in dosed AD patients; contra on that readout, low confidence.
engagement.magnitude_basis: serum total IgE, day 29 and day 140 vs baseline (no change)

dose.note: Genetic-deletion models imply complete pathway loss as the target; no antibody exposure target was ever stated for AD.
dose.short: Knockouts imply full neutralization; no target
dose.quote: IL-25 and IL-33 are the predominant ILC2-inducing cytokines in this model.
dose.judgement: Li 2017 (doi:10.1038/cddis.2017.90) later showed significantly less MC903 dermatitis in IL-33-/- and ST2-/- mice, so the implied exposure target is full neutralization; none of the four antibodies binds mouse IL-33, so no mouse antibody dose-response exists.

efficacy.model: IL1RL1 AD-GWAS locus and IL33 loss-of-function carriers
efficacy.note: Japanese AD GWAS placed a risk locus at IL1RL1-IL18R1-IL18RAP (P=8e-18); the causal gene inside it was not resolved.
efficacy.short: AD GWAS hits the ST2 locus
efficacy.quote: …we report here 8 new susceptibility loci: IL1RL1-IL18R1-IL18RAP (P(combined) = 8.36 × 10(-18)), the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region (P = 8.38 × 10(-20)) …
efficacy.confidence_note: Quote is the opening clause of a sentence longer than 40 words; abstract-level.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the human-genetic track in AD. The locus is shared by three receptor genes and has a small odds ratio; the IL33 loss-of-function variant (Smith 2017) protects from asthma, with no AD phenotype reported.

efficacy.note: ST2/IL-33-driven ILC2s promote MC903 AD-like inflammation in mice; Li 2017 extended this to IL-33-/- and ST2-/- knockouts.
efficacy.quote: IL-25 and IL-33 are the predominant ILC2-inducing cytokines in this model.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the mouse track. The class prediction is that neutralizing IL-33 should reduce eczema; Li 2017 (doi:10.1038/cddis.2017.90) made it explicit: 'These data suggest that IL-33/IL-33R may be a therapeutic target of AD.'

efficacy.note: ATLAS (~300 patients, four etokimab regimens): every arm missed EASI change at week 16 vs placebo; registry later showed all p>0.4.
efficacy.short: Every etokimab arm missed EASI week 16
efficacy.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.
efficacy.confidence_note: The press release (filed as 8-K exhibit 99.2 on 2019-11-08) is the only prose record; ClinicalTrials.gov results posted 2023-05-24 confirm every arm, and the trial was never peer-reviewed. trial_unreported marks that absence of a peer-reviewed report.
efficacy.judgement: Year is 2019 because the press release made the result public on 2019-11-08; the tier 3 registry record (2023-05-24) sets the status and agrees. Paired myself with Salimi 2013/Li 2017: the knockouts predicted less eczema with IL-33 loss; the antibody gave none over a 49% placebo improvement. Two later facts belong on this track but are not scored as entries: Pietka 2020 (Sci Rep, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-63410-z, received 2020-01-28, after the ATLAS failure) found IL-33-/-, ST2-/- and double-knockout mice develop MC903 dermatitis like wild type, a retrodiction that agrees with patients but cannot flip a contra track without patient_signal_reversed; and Chen 2026 (MAbs) showed etokimab and itepekimab only partially block ST2, a post-hoc explanation that does not rescue the class because tozorakimab, which blocks fully, also failed (Silverberg 2025).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: registry: placebo-adjusted % change in EASI at week 16 = +7.8, -6.3, +2.0, +4.8 points (p 0.45-0.83); placebo arm -49%

patient_trials.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.

efficacy.model: House-dust-mite skin challenge in AD patients (single-dose etokimab)
efficacy.note: Twelve-patient open-label etokimab study: 83% EASI50 after one dose plus the HDM-challenge neutrophil signal, read as therapeutic potential in AD.
efficacy.quote: These human in vivo findings confirm an IL-33 upstream role in modulating skin inflammatory cascades and define the therapeutic potential for IL-33 inhibition in human diseases, including AD.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the clinical EASI arm was uncontrolled, only the challenge readout had a placebo comparison.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the human-challenge track in the same year its prediction was tested.

efficacy.model: House-dust-mite skin challenge in AD patients (single-dose etokimab)
efficacy.note: The challenge study's predicted benefit disappeared in ATLAS: placebo-controlled EASI change at week 16 was no better than placebo in any arm.
efficacy.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.
efficacy.confidence_note: Same press release and registry record as the mouse-track entry.
efficacy.judgement: Kept as a separate track because it is a different system with its own prediction (human challenge, not mouse). The challenge arm measured HDM-evoked neutrophils, not eczema, and the EASI arm had no placebo; ATLAS's 49% placebo improvement swallowed the open-label signal.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: open-label 83% EASI50 after one dose vs ATLAS placebo-adjusted EASI change of about zero

patient_trials.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.

efficacy.model: IL1RL1 AD-GWAS locus and IL33 loss-of-function carriers
efficacy.note: The GWAS-implicated ST2/IL-33 axis did not translate: four antibodies against IL-33 missed their AD phase 2 primary endpoints from 2019.
efficacy.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.
efficacy.confidence_note: A common-variant locus shared with IL18R1/IL18RAP predicts pathway involvement, not an effect size, and the IL33 loss-of-function variant is an asthma finding; scored contra under the direction rule, flagged low.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: a GWAS locus is a weak prediction and the task names it as rationale, so it is scored on its own human-genetic track at low confidence rather than folded into the mouse track. Pairing is mine; no source puts the genetics beside the trial.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of the class prediction (pathway causal in AD) vs placebo-adjusted EASI change of about zero

patient_trials.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.

efficacy.reason: Pathway genetics did not predict efficacy

efficacy.note: Itepekimab's two AD trials were terminated after a failed interim; torudokimab and tozorakimab missed too, with the source doubting IL-33 drives AD.
efficacy.quote: The lack of clinical efficacy for itepekimab observed in these studies suggests that IL-33 may not be a key pathogenic driver in moderate-to-severe AD.
efficacy.confidence_note: Itepekimab's posted registry numbers (300 mg q4w -80% vs placebo -33.5% EASI) are from arms of about 10 after early termination; the program stopped on the companion proof-of-concept interim (NCT03736967), and the tier 1 paper sets the status.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2019 contra with a tier 1 source and the three later trials: torudokimab NCT03831191 (terminated for lack of efficacy at interim, results 2021-04-20; the task's NCT04469530 is a sirolimus oncology trial, corrected here), itepekimab NCT03738423 (lack of efficacy, 2022-06-10) and tozorakimab FRONTIER-2 NCT04212169 (Silverberg 2025, doi:10.1111/jdv.20388, primary p 0.55-0.89). The COPD programs for itepekimab and tozorakimab continued and are not AD evidence.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: registry: torudokimab vIGA 0/1 at week 16 5.0/5.9/4.8% vs 9.5% placebo (NCT03831191); tozorakimab EASI difference +1.3/+5.9/-1.7 points, p 0.55-0.89 (Silverberg 2025)

patient_trials.quote: The lack of clinical efficacy for itepekimab observed in these studies suggests that IL-33 may not be a key pathogenic driver in moderate-to-severe AD.
The study was terminated for lack of efficacy after an interim analysis was performed
FRONTIER-2 did not show a statistically significant difference in the primary endpoint for tozorakimab compared with placebo.

efficacy.model: Anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody in DNCB-induced AD mice (Peng 2018)
efficacy.note: A neutralising anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody given after each DNCB challenge improved lesions, scratching, ear thickness and dermatitis score; read as curative for AD.
efficacy.short: Antibody cured DNCB dermatitis in mice
efficacy.quote: Our study suggests that blockade of IL-33 has a curative effect on AD.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled): 14 subcutaneous antibody doses over 33 days, tacrolimus as comparator; antibody clone, dose and effect sizes not in the abstract. Online 2017-09-26 (Crossref), print February 2018.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the only prospective pharmacological AD-model track for the class: none of the four members binds mouse IL-33, so a surrogate anti-mouse antibody is the closest any animal came to the dosed product (product_in_model false). The same paper correlates serum IL-33/sST2 with human AD activity, a biomarker association that predicts nothing about treatment and is not scored.

efficacy.model: Anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody in DNCB-induced AD mice (Peng 2018)
efficacy.note: ATLAS: no etokimab arm beat placebo on EASI change at week 16 (placebo -49%), where antibody-dosed DNCB mice had predicted a curative effect.
efficacy.short: Curative in mice, no arm beat placebo
efficacy.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.
efficacy.confidence_note: Patient side is the 2019-11-08 press release (tier 5; ClinicalTrials.gov results posted 2023-05-24 confirm every arm, no peer-reviewed report). Model side abstract-only. Paired myself: a neutralising antibody that 'cured' hapten dermatitis in mice vs a neutralising antibody with no placebo-adjusted effect in patients.
efficacy.judgement: Direct pharmacological miss: the model dosed an antibody of the same mechanism (species-matched surrogate) and predicted benefit; the first member trial with a placebo arm gave none. Year 2019 from the press release, status set by the tier 3 registry record, matching the draft's convention for the ATLAS entry.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: registry NCT03533751: placebo-adjusted % change in EASI at week 16 = +7.8, -6.3, +2.0, +4.8 points (p 0.45-0.83); placebo arm -49%

patient_trials.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.

efficacy.model: Anti-mouse-IL-33 antibody in DNCB-induced AD mice (Peng 2018)
efficacy.note: Torudokimab's AD trial was stopped for lack of efficacy at interim (vIGA 0/1 5-6% vs 9.5% placebo); itepekimab and tozorakimab missed after it.
efficacy.short: Three more antibodies, three more misses
efficacy.quote: The study was terminated for lack of efficacy after an interim analysis was performed
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry whyStopped text read directly (results posted 2021-04-20); Laquer 2022 BJD (10.1111/bjd.21631) is the tier 1 report but is a research letter without an abstract and was not opened. Itepekimab (Kosloski 2024, 10.1111/cts.13874) and tozorakimab FRONTIER-2 (Silverberg 2025, 10.1111/jdv.20388) are carried as patient_trials.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2019 miss with a second member and a tier 3 record (year 2021 per rule 7: the second miss was public 2021-04-20, before the 2024 paper). The surrogate-antibody mouse prediction failed for every member tested with a placebo arm.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: registry NCT03831191: vIGA 0/1 at week 16 5.0/5.9/4.8% vs 9.5% placebo; FRONTIER-2 EASI difference +1.3/+5.9/-1.7 points, p 0.55-0.89 (Silverberg 2025)

patient_trials.quote: The study was terminated for lack of efficacy after an interim analysis was performed
The lack of clinical efficacy for itepekimab observed in these studies suggests that IL-33 may not be a key pathogenic driver in moderate-to-severe AD.
FRONTIER-2 did not show a statistically significant difference in the primary endpoint for tozorakimab compared with placebo.

efficacy.model: Stat6VT spontaneous-AD mice with IL-33 deficiency (DaSilva-Arnold 2018)
efficacy.note: IL-33 loss made spontaneous AD-like disease worse in Stat6VT mice: the one pre-trial AD model predicting no benefit, if anything harm, from IL-33 blockade.
efficacy.quote: Furthermore, AD-like disease was more severe in IL-33-deficient Stat6VT mice compared to IL-33-sufficient Stat6VT mice.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMC release 2019-04-01, not opened); epub 2018-01-24, received 2017-07-10. Severity measure and group sizes not in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Own track: a T-cell STAT6-driven spontaneous model crossed to IL-33 knockout is a different system from the MC903 transgenic/knockout track and predicted the opposite direction (IL-33 protective), so it cannot share that track's score.

efficacy.model: Stat6VT spontaneous-AD mice with IL-33 deficiency (DaSilva-Arnold 2018)
efficacy.note: ATLAS matched the Stat6VT prediction of no benefit: no etokimab arm beat placebo on EASI at week 16; the predicted worsening did not appear, so direction only.
efficacy.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired myself from an abstract-level mouse paper and a tier 5 release (registry results 2023-05-24 confirm). The match is on direction only: the mice also predicted worsening, and every etokimab arm improved about as much as placebo (-49%), so the harm half of the prediction was not borne out.
efficacy.judgement: same with direction_only rather than neg: neg needs the model's own number for a class member below a class effect bar, and no member was ever dosed in this system nor did the class establish an effect bar, so neg is unearnable here. Not also scored in safety: the predicted harm is the treated disease itself and is counted once, here. Itepekimab (NCT03738423, 2022-06-10), torudokimab (NCT03831191, 2021-04-20) and tozorakimab (NCT04212169, Silverberg 2025) repeated the no-benefit result.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: registry NCT03533751: placebo-adjusted % change in EASI at week 16 = +7.8, -6.3, +2.0, +4.8 points (p 0.45-0.83), i.e. no benefit and no worsening

patient_trials.quote: Each of the etokimab dosing arms failed to meet the primary endpoint of the trial, which was demonstration of statistically greater improvement in the Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) relative placebo at week 16.
The study was terminated for lack of efficacy after an interim analysis was performed
The lack of clinical efficacy for itepekimab observed in these studies suggests that IL-33 may not be a key pathogenic driver in moderate-to-severe AD.
FRONTIER-2 did not show a statistically significant difference in the primary endpoint for tozorakimab compared with placebo.

safety.model: Cynomolgus PK and IL-1-family specificity panel (torudokimab)
safety.note: The only published preclinical safety-relevant statement for the class: IL-1-family specificity and cynomolgus PK; no toxicology data in print.
safety.short: Specific for IL-33; cyno PK only
safety.quote: Torudokimab is highly specific to IL-33 and does not bind any of the other IL-1 family members.
safety.judgement: No animal toxicology for any of the four antibodies is published and none binds mouse IL-33, so the mouse models made no safety prediction and are left out of this cell; the quotable model-side prediction is specificity plus cynomolgus PK, which predicts a selective, tolerable antibody.

safety.model: Cynomolgus PK and IL-1-family specificity panel (torudokimab)
safety.note: Itepekimab was well tolerated alone and with dupilumab in AD; registry AE tables for etokimab, torudokimab and tozorakimab show no arm-level signal.
safety.short: No safety signal in four AD trials
safety.quote: Itepekimab was generally well tolerated, both alone and in combination with dupilumab.
safety.confidence_note: Different molecule from the model source; 16-week phase 2 exposure only; torudokimab 600 mg had 2 serious adverse events (registry) with none attributed; Silverberg 2025 adds 'tozorakimab was well tolerated'.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: scored same at low confidence rather than untested because a stated prediction (selective, tolerable) held in every AD trial; a mouse cannot show immunogenicity or injection-site effects and the mice never saw these antibodies, so their silence is not a miss. IL-33/ST2 double-knockout mice are viable (Pietka 2020), consistent with no on-target harm, but that was never stated as a safety prediction.
safety.magnitude_basis: adverse-event profile vs placebo over 16 weeks
safety.reason: Predicted clean antibody; trials were clean
